facebook.content_angle: Flip turn time loss — how most club swimmers bleed 2 seconds at every wall through a slow push-off and miss the fastest free metres in every lap
facebook.post_text:
You're losing 2 seconds at every wall. Every single lap. 🚨

Most club swimmers treat the turn as a transition — a moment to reset. Elite swimmers treat it as an acceleration phase. That gap in thinking is costing you more time than a bad stroke ever could.

👉 A weak push-off drops your velocity to near zero before you've even started kicking
👉 A shallow turn angle forces a longer, slower rotation that kills momentum
👉 Most swimmers exit the wall at half the speed they entered it

In a 200m freestyle, that's potentially 8 seconds lost to walls alone. 😤

✔️ Drive your feet into the wall at shoulder width — not together, not wide
✔️ Push off deep enough to stay below surface turbulence for 1.5 metres
✔️ Hold your streamline tight until you hit race pace before taking your first stroke

Your wall is either your secret weapon or your biggest leak. Right now, which one is it for you?
facebook.engagement_bait: Drop a ⏱️ if you know your turns are costing you time
facebook.call_to_action: Which part of your turn do you think is leaking the most time — the rotation, the push-off, or the streamline?
